review: Humanoid text and each nonhumanoid table cell transcribed; B553 column alignment and notes visually checked against the rendered page. Full location procedure, rounding, critical effects and body-form integration remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Random hit location uses three dice against the target's actual body form. Deliberate targeting uses the specified penalty and must validate existence, exposure, angle and damage-type eligibility.
A randomly selected missing body part becomes a torso hit. This fallback does not make deliberate attacks on nonexistent parts legal.
A deliberate eye, skull, face, groin, neck or vitals attack that misses by exactly one hits the torso instead; do not generalize this to every body location.

Eye targeting permits impaling, piercing or tight-beam burning from front or side. Injury greater than one-tenth maximum health blinds the eye; otherwise use skull treatment without the skull's additional resistance.
Skull supplies two extra resistance, quadruple wounding and knockdown at -10; criticals use the head table. The printed toxic-damage exception must be applied through the detailed location procedure.

Face ignores an open-faced helmet's resistance, uses knockdown -5 and the head critical table. Corrosion has multiplier 1.5 and a major wound blinds one eye, or both when injury exceeds full maximum health. Random rear face hits become skull hits.

Limb hits reduce large/huge piercing and impaling multipliers to one. A single injury above half maximum health cripples the limb; apply the general rounding and excess-injury cap rather than subtracting unlimited global health.
A shield-bearing limb is deliberately targeted at -4 and its extremity at -8. Apply only to the relevant shield-covered limb rather than every limb of the character.
For applicable male anatomy, crushing groin damage doubles shock and gives knockdown -5. Otherwise use torso effects; anatomical eligibility is explicit, not inferred from display text.
Extremities follow limb wounding but a single injury above one-third maximum health cripples them; cap excess injury through the general injury procedure.
Where the table marks a paired location, one die 1-3 selects right and 4-6 left; do not reroll an already specified side.
Neck crushing/corrosion uses multiplier 1.5 and cutting uses two. Decapitation on a fatal cutting neck hit is an explicit author option.
Vitals permit impaling/piercing at triple wounding and tight-beam burning at double wounding; other attack types cannot target them.

Diffuse anatomy ignores location-specific shock, knockdown and wounding multipliers while still allowing eye/limb/extremity crippling. Impaling/piercing injury is capped at one, other attacks at two, subject to detailed area-effect exceptions.
Homogeneous anatomy ignores special location shock, knockdown and wound multipliers while retaining eye/limb/extremity crippling. Apply its damage-type factors from the separate rows.
Without a brain, skull and face have no special knockdown or wounding modifier. Eye hits can blind but otherwise use face rather than skull treatment.
Without vital organs, vitals and groin hits use torso treatment; preserve actual anatomy and any separate restrictions on deliberate targeting.
Nonliving anatomy retains location effects but reduces impaling/piercing multipliers outside eyes, skull and vitals. Its reduced factors must not override those exceptional locations.
For an upright body with wings, random nine selects a randomly chosen wing and ten remains torso. Wings are deliberately targeted at -2 and use limb injury.
For an upright fish-tailed form, random leg results become torso and foot results become tail. Deliberate tail targeting is -3 and uses aquatic-tail injury.
For the upright/four-leg hybrid, random nine/ten hit the lower animal torso and eleven the upper humanoid torso. Either torso can be deliberately targeted without penalty.
For the hybrid's random extremity, one die 1-2 selects upper hand, 3-4 forefoot, 5-6 hind foot; odd is left and even right. This differs from the ordinary paired-side roll.

A grasping, striking or fish tail cripples as a limb; an ordinary tail as an extremity. A crippled tail gives land creatures -1 dexterity, swimmers/flyers -2 dexterity and half movement. Missing or very short tails convert random hits to torso.
Wings cripple as limbs, and a crippled wing prevents flight. Falling and recovery must use the actual airborne state rather than only changing a movement number.
Winged serpents replace random 15-18 with wing at -2 deliberate targeting.
An armed serpentine form replaces 7-8 with right arm, 13-14 with left arm, and 17-18 with hand; deliberate arm/hand penalties are -2/-4.
The squid variation changes 17-18 to torso. Arms other than the first pair are extremities for injury and targeted at -3, overriding the base eight-arm table.
The scorpion variation changes random twelve to tail, deliberately targeted at -3.
An eight-arm creature's first four arms are its current manipulators and last four its current locomotor limbs; anatomy state must identify the actual limb roles.
The brain location for specified nonhumanoid forms uses skull effects but only one extra resistance.
A fish-like form selects randomly among its actual fins when a fin is hit. Fins cripple as extremities and a crippled fin gives -3 dexterity; specify duration through injury recovery.
Pincer-bodied forms select among actual true legs for a random leg result. Their forelimb pincers are arms, not generic legs.
An eight-leg body identifies front, middle-front, middle-back and rear pairs as legs 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 and 7-8 respectively.
homogeneous impaling wound multiplier is 1/2 where that injury model applies; preserve its location exceptions.
homogeneous huge-piercing wound multiplier is 1/2 where that injury model applies; preserve its location exceptions.
homogeneous large-piercing wound multiplier is 1/3 where that injury model applies; preserve its location exceptions.
homogeneous piercing wound multiplier is 1/5 where that injury model applies; preserve its location exceptions.
homogeneous small-piercing wound multiplier is 1/10 where that injury model applies; preserve its location exceptions.
nonliving impaling wound multiplier is 1/1 where that injury model applies; preserve its location exceptions.
nonliving huge-piercing wound multiplier is 1/1 where that injury model applies; preserve its location exceptions.
nonliving large-piercing wound multiplier is 1/2 where that injury model applies; preserve its location exceptions.
nonliving piercing wound multiplier is 1/3 where that injury model applies; preserve its location exceptions.
nonliving small-piercing wound multiplier is 1/5 where that injury model applies; preserve its location exceptions.
